sha-tate-shafarevich-group: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Sha D e is defined from an LData D: the places of F above l, a chosen place of the algebraic closure over each, and a character chi of GS extending the cyclotomic character (unique, since G_F maps onto GS). GS is the quotient of G_F by the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups at finite places outside S, so the archimedean places impose no condition. shaLen is a length in the extended naturals. The independence of the choice of places is proved here; the Lean states it as the proposition Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Indep and avoids it by requiring every bound for every LData.
sha-plus-minus: The involution is UpperTheory.V.galoisActionOnCohomology for IsCMField.complexConj, defined through any lift of complex conjugation (h1TwistConjByLift) and shown independent of the lift. ShaPlus and ShaMinus are defined for every natural number e.
sha-plus-minus-length: The Lean proves the splitting for any module with an involution over a ring in which 2 is a unit (length_eq_add_eigen) and applies it with s = (-1)^e.
sha-bounded-field: VVle, VVplusLe and VVminusLe quantify over an algebraic closure and a family of LData, one for each prime; the sums use ENat.toNat of the lengths, and finiteness is asserted separately for 0 < k < t, so the sums are those of the text. The 2-bound is VVat 2 (also called BoundedHeightTwoPlaceCondition).
sha-vandiver-weakening: VWin is the proposition that VWinAt psi 401 holds for every primitive character psi; it is a hypothesis of the zero-free statements of Chapter 13 and is proved in Theorem sha-weakening-from-galois-representations. PageN is the condition on e. The announcement's footnote 6 says that vanishing of a number of K-groups of Z should follow; no statement about K-groups is formalized, and none is made here.
sha-abelian-field: AbF records m and H; AbF.ker a means that a mod m lies in H. Fields of a datum, composita and host fields are all given by an embedding into CyclotomicField N together with the description of the fixing automorphisms. condF is an infimum of natural numbers and is 0 when the set is empty, which does not happen for the fields considered.
sha-composita: Part (a) is isCompField_ofChar; part (b) combines isCMField_of_isChiField (which assumes q prime with q % 4 = 3) and conductor_bounds_of_isChiField; part (c) is UpperTheory.V.Odd.deg, proved as in the text.
sha-bernoulli-bound: Related to the published theorems, not a special case. Mazur-Wiles and Rubin bound the odd eigenspaces of class groups of abelian fields by Bernoulli numbers; the Lean statement PsiBound bounds eigenspaces of Tate-Shafarevich groups of Tate twists over abelian CM fields by the normalized Bernoulli number N times the primorial of k+2 times B_{k+1,chi}, with coefficients in a finite DVR inside the algebraic closure of Q_l. It is vacuous when that number does not lie in O. The Lean proves it (UpperTheory.V.ML.iv, through ML.recip and ML.psiOf) from Poitou-Tate duality and unramified orthogonality, both proved results; the mapping pass describes the argument as an Euler system of Gauss sums.
sha-minus-prime-to-degree: UpperTheory.V.Odd.PrimeBound, proved by primeBound_of from PsiBound and the lemmas actEx, actFacts, prodVal and atPrime. The constant is bnd N (k+1) = 16 N^(k+2) (k+1)!.
sha-minus-exponent: StickBound C, proved by stickBound = stick_of killPow lenPow gen. killPow gives the exponent r with constant 30 (bdxLog, through bdX_mul_le), and stick_of multiplies by the constant 8 of gen, so the Lean's constant is 240. The hypothesis on l is Procyc: l odd, or the cyclotomic character modulo 4 trivial on G_E.
sha-minus-part: ThmBcFree, with the bound minusBound C o n N t. The Lean also states the version for admitted exponent functions, ThmBc, and proves the two equivalent (thmBc_iff); the main proof uses ThmBc.
sha-ferrero-washington: The Lean statement bounds the order of Cl(K')/Cl(K')^l for every l^n-th cyclotomic extension K' of K; this is equivalent to the vanishing of the mu-invariant, but the equivalence is not in the Lean. It is proved in the Lean (UpperTheory.V.FW.ferreroWashington) from Stickelberger's theorem and the nonvanishing modulo l of twisted half Stickelberger elements (UpperTheory.V.FW.nonvan), after embedding K in a cyclotomic field.
sha-tower-data: In ABound the field K is any normed field over Q_l with ultrametric norm. The Tate-Shafarevich groups of layers are written shaInv L1 l k in the Lean, defined through ShaAbs over the algebraic closure; this text identifies them with the groups of Definition sha-tate-shafarevich-group. The H^2 in (ii) is VLen D k, the length of H^2(GS, Z_l(k+1)) for an LData D of L2.
sha-tower-bounds: FixedIn and TwoIn, proved by UpperTheory.V.Two.fixedIn and twoIn from Ferrero-Washington and TowerBound = aBound_of_isTower (Lemma sha-tower-from-module). For (a), towerFixed takes R = max 1 r with r from fwRk. For (b), the 2-base is a field of base2 M q d = (withI M) sup (quad q) sup (quad d) (twoBase: degBasic for the degree, layerFn for L1, compIndex for E inside L1 with index dividing 2, shaTwo with kerTwo for the comparison), and towerTwo gives R = 4(g + 6 deg M) through baseRk: charStep with orbTwo (at most 2 deg M primes above q and 4 deg M above d) and quadStep through idxTwo. AbF.sup is the join written A v B in the text.
sha-soule-bound: LemmaK CK, with the bound kBound CK k [L:Q] |d_L| = exp((2k[L:Q])^CK log(2|d_L|)). Proved by UpperTheory.V.ZK.lemmaK through lemmaK_of_steps, which takes the 21 step propositions as hypotheses and is applied to their proofs: SLayer (Lemma sha-enlarging), SSha (Lemma sha-kummer-descent), SCount (Lemma sha-count-homs), SFew (Lemma sha-few-norms, assembled by SFewOf from STheta, SPhi, SClass, SUpper and SDetect), STors (Lemma sha-gl-torsion), and the numerical steps sNum (Step 1) and sFinal (Step 2). The Lean's sNum takes the constant 5 (max C0 9 + 2) + 11 for Step 1. sFinal uses GlobalTheory.Published.PoitouTateDuality, LocalFinitenessK and LocalTateDualityK, through LDataCardLeFinrank.VLen_le_shaLen_add. Soule proved finiteness of these H^2 through K-theory and bounded torsion in the homology of GL_N(Z) by perfect forms; the statement here is new and follows his method.
sha-window-pigeonhole: UpperTheory.V.Win.window, with Good eta Ct Exc x as the conclusion; the induction is window1. Exc is a finite set of natural numbers and may contain 0.
sha-window-constants: BConst, BConst.R, BConst.J, admitted and IsBWindow (InRange together with BaAt and BbAt); a controlled window is IsBWindow. BaAt is the 2-bound for composita, BbAt the l-bound for layers of degree l^(log_l R_l + 3).

Its hypotheses are Poitou-Tate duality, LocalFinitenessK, LocalTateDualityK, Ferrero-Washington and Lemma K, all proved; the theorems LiteratureTheorems.poitou_tate_normalised_of_open, local_finiteness_k_of_open and local_tate_duality_k_of_open do not use their open-image hypothesis. The condition on B' is OddPrimesWithRootsOfUnity.
sha-character-parts: UpperTheory.V.Chr.VS l n e theta is the length of ShaU (rho l e theta) n, the classes of H^1(G_Q, O tensor Q_l/Z_l) with action theta^(-1) chi_cyc^(-e) that vanish on the decomposition groups at the places where n has positive valuation and on all inertia groups. V is VS with n = l; Vlen is VS with n = l N for the modulus N of the host. Vn divides the length by eO, the ramification index of O.
sha-plus-by-characters: Part (a) is redPrime, part (b) is redAll with lambda = lossAll l N [E:Q] k = Chr.loss l N n k + omega(N) v_l(n), where Chr.loss l N n k = (n + n^2) nuBound l N k + omega(N) (n v_l(n)) and nuBound is the number nu of the text. lossLe gives lambda at most (Nk)^6 when 2 <= N, n <= N and k >= 1. Step 1 is partModel and signLe; Step 2 is eigLe (selTwist, selDown, cokerAb, kerIdx, kerFin and H0_local_card_bounded_of_cls_ker_le_ker), with eigV for equality when l does not divide n; Step 3 is vLe, used through V_le_V'. The field E is described by Chr.HasLevel E N H.
sha-trivial-character: PropZ, proved by UpperTheory.V.X.propZ. The case l-1 | k is zOne, which uses hom_kill (Kronecker-Weber) and control (Lemma sha-control); the other case is zQuad, which uses the bound h < l for the class number of the real quadratic field of discriminant l (hQuad).
sha-ordinary-deformation: Eisenstein data are GD; deformation data are UpperTheory.V.U3.Dat, which also fixes an embedding of the algebraic closure into that of Q_l, the local field K_v cut out by eta, and continuity conditions. GG 3 R is GL_3(R) semidirect {+1,-1}, with -1 acting by theta(g) = J g^(-T) J. Ordinary points are OrdPt: Red (multiplier eta and reduction to r0), AdicCont, Normalised, the condition away from l, and CondT at B. The components of a Dirichlet character at a prime are defined through idempotents of Z/N (comp, th0, chiP).
sha-residually-reducible-automorphy: GdEndAlt asks for g1 with Marks (which also records c^2 = 1, eta(c) = -1 and Psi(c) = 1), FinEnd, AutEnd3Alt and AutEnd2Ao. AutEnd3Alt asks for irreducibility on every open subgroup of ker eta; statement (ii) asks only for irreducibility on ker eta (TypeI), as Aut.AutBAlt does, the form used downstream (AutomorphyUnramifiedCoefficientsAlt, derived from GdEndAlt by automorphyUnramified_of_locPrints_kisin_gdEnd). The two are bridged by Pr.matIrr_open_gd, which is the paragraph on irreducibility on open subgroups in the proof. AutBAlt is phrased for the Qbar_l-points of the universal ring D.Ring with unramified coefficients (eO = 1), which exists_ordPt_of_point turns into ordinary points over a discrete valuation ring, conjugate to the given one. Windowed is WitA, through Unl1, PotUnl and WinAt; for W it is WitAQ. Attachment to a cuspidal representation is AttC, and to a newform Af.Newform.Att. The plan describes the stable points through a definite U(3); the Lean asserts conjugate self-dual cuspidal automorphy for GL_3 over K. The Lean proves GdEndAlt as the first half of Z.Win.Dn.ends0_alt from HypothesesH', built from the literature hypothesis whose only unproved input is Row0b. The propositions of the proof are Sd.Seed2Alt (seed2_alt), Z.Sym.UnitaryThreeAutomorphyDense (unitary_three_automorphy_dense_of_prints), Z.Sym.Pl.LinkedEndEAlt (linkedEnd_alt), Z.J.LinkedUnlE (linkedUnlE_holds_alt) and ends_of_alt. The published inputs are the hypotheses LiteratureRankNHypothesis (LitLocAlt, LiteratureAutomorphyHypothesis, LitCoh, LiteratureCMHypothesis) and the fields of Af.Hypotheses' and HypothesesH' (ClozelCohC, ClozelConjC, BorelInjC, GaloisRepExistsTotallyRealGL2, StrongMultOneReal, GelfandKazhdanReal, AdmissibleReal, QuadBC0, NewformRep, DescWeak, CycC, Desc2, DefQuatExists, CuspSemisimpleReal); a textual dependency search from ends0_alt, through about 60,000 declarations, reaches about 130 statements in the Published namespaces (among them BaseChangeDefiniteUnitary, CaraianiLocalGlobal, GaloisRepOfPolarizedCuspidal, GreenbergWiles and BlochKatoLocal) and no automorphy lifting theorem. The automorphy of ordinary points is proved in the Lean: Hi.hida_unitary_of_printed_hida constructs a Hecke ideal J of the universal ordinary determinant ring from unitary Hecke data, Pa.PfromAut with Pa.TaylorWilesObstructionBound gives the patching bound, and W.modU_of_printsH gives ModUAlt. The method is of the kind used for residually reducible representations by Skinner and Wiles and by Thorne, but no published lifting theorem is invoked, so none is cited. In the text, a link is Pr.GalLink (with Fr.Frame for the data Gamma, the places above l and the characters; upl L is Gal(Qbar/L^+)), the residual conditions are Frame.Ok C0 and Frame.Big C0, a seed datum is Pr.SeedClause (with Sd.FieldPairCharacterTripleConditions; its quadratic field is K, since eta' = eta), linked points are Fr.NRep lifts with the inertial characters Psi^(w n i), and the existence of a link with seeds for each Eisenstein datum is Fr.gd_ex (GdFrameEx). The universal ordinary determinant ring is W.UniversalOrdinaryDeterminantRing, the Hecke ideal property is HidaPropsAlt (ring, dense, pt, end1, end2, twist), and the patching bound is P1core and P3core (formal arcs x : Point r over k[[T]], nice of type I or E); ModUAlt combines them. The descent step is gdEnd_of_frame_linkedEnd_downCsdK_descent, with DownCsdKAlt (descent along solvable extensions), RankTwoAutomorphyDescendsFromAbelianCMToRat and AutNewformA, all proved from the published hypotheses. The Hecke ideal and the patching bound are Propositions sha-hecke-ideal and sha-patching-bound, stated before the theorem with the steps of their proofs as the lemmas sha-hecke-data, sha-hecke-algebra, sha-hecke-determinant and sha-patching-normalization to sha-patching-chain. The proof of (b), adjoint_lift_from_eisenstein_of_propagation, uses an adjoint lift between definite unitary groups in two and three variables (AdLiftW), proved in the Lean, and a textual dependency search finds neither the Hecke ideal nor the patching bound below it; they enter (c) and (d). The automorphy of the adjoint lift is related to the theorem of Gelbart and Jacquet, which the Lean does not use. The statement (b) in the proof takes from UnitaryThreeAutomorphyDense the hypotheses on M (2 l | M, UnrSplit L M, chi' unramified on Gal(Qbar/L) away from M), and its conclusion Sd.IsSeedAlt includes the windowed condition (Z.Win.IsAutCsdA). In (d), J.TanA, the existence of two independent tangent vectors in step (5), is a hypothesis of UnitaryRankTwoFlagsAlt and of linkedUnlE_alt; linkedUnlE_holds_alt discharges it by J.tanA from GC.Hypotheses₂ (the published Galois cohomology inputs of the literature hypothesis, with GreenbergWiles) and Loc.LocalPublishedTheorems, so neither (d) nor the theorem assumes it. In (d)(1) the map phi of OpenEx2EAlt is onto the subalgebra Fr.Space.B of the ring of linked points (the closure of the algebra generated by the weight-zero monomials mon 0 and the inertial characters), not onto the whole ring.

UpperTheory.V.AlgebraTools.jqTheta, for any homomorphism theta that agrees with the double coset operators hk on the Dom elements (thetaEx gives the unique one). The Lean states it with the normalized action jacB of the torus on the Jacquet module, jacB(t) = deltaHalf(t)^{-1} times the action of t, as q(theta t v) = deltaHalf(t)^{-1} jacB(t) q(v); deltaHalf is the square root of modulus, the product of the |t_i|^{modExp i}, which is the modulus character delta. The book states the equivalent unnormalized form.

UpperTheory.V.AlgebraTools.jqInj, for every subgroup C. Borel's theorem [Bor76] is the published statement for the Iwahori subgroup (the Iwahori-fixed vectors map isomorphically onto the invariants of the integral torus in the Jacquet module); the Lean proves the injectivity for every I_C its own way, through the invertibility of the dominant operators (domMul).

sha-automorphy-realization: (1) is Pr.IsKa (alg, conj with sigma, unr, ord). (2) is Pr.CReal: C_0, ok and big for Phi.ext f; the HidaSetting s with its level V (hV), the residual datum r (W.Resid), the twisted link K (Pr.TwLink: pi, e, lam and kappa, with pi_pr, kappa_pr, lam_j and A_pl; the text lists all its fields: kappa_cont, kappa_conj, ramκ, tame, mu (mu_v in the closure of the commutator subgroup of G_v, used in Lemmas sha-automorphy-realization-components-transfer-twist and sha-automorphy-realization-seed) and ker (the kernel of pi in every closed normal subgroup N of G_0 stable under conj that contains I0 and the elements of the Iu u at which Psi-bar o pi is 1, used by the private untwist of SeedOf.lean)), v0 (r.V0ok) with v0M, the universal ordinary determinant ring B_0 and the space S (Fr.Space, with its universal property univ). (3): a compatible map is Setup.IsPhi. (4): an off-triangular prime p is one with S.u.TI p (Fr.NRep.TI: OffTri, through triP and triM, and for n = 3 not ee <= p), for p a prime of S.A, as in AllGood. The text's A_n is S.R; B is S.B (Fr.Space.B, the adic closure of the O_1-subalgebra generated by S.rho.mon 0 and all the values of the S.rho.psi v i); A_n^circ is S.A (Fr.Space.A, generated by S.B and the entries). A compatible map goes from B_0 to S.B.
sha-automorphy-realization-twists: UpperTheory.V.Pr.kaOf (Pr.KaOf), from Sd.AlgCyc and Sd.AlgRes. The hypothesis on kappa is Sd.IsTwist iota sigma kappa; the text lists the fields that the proof uses (alg, conj, unr, ord). The proof follows the Lean.
sha-automorphy-realization-exists: Pr.coefEx gives O_1 (W.Large L c_1 and the values of the twists) and the residue map; Pr.CRealEx and cRealAv (from W.LevEx and W.ProModularRingExists) give the realizations, with not (R.s.p divides p_0). The text splits the statement: (1) is Pr.CoefEx, for any coefficient ring c in place of O (as openEx2E_alt uses it), and (2) is CRealAv, whose hypotheses on c_1 are c.O <= c_1.O, the residue map, IsKa and the values of kappa in c_1.O (Large is not needed). The proofs follow the Lean. In (2), the fields mu and ker of the TwLink are steps (j) (cr_mu, through Loc.muNone, which the Lean proves from local class field theory; the text cites it) and (k) (frame_criterion_kernel); its fields ramκ and tame are proved in step (e); the universal rings come from the hypothesis W.ProModularRingExists, proved as W.b0Ex from W.phiAll (Lemma sha-automorphy-realization-exists-determinant), applied to the residual pair, and from Fr.space_ex (Lemma sha-automorphy-realization-exists-linked).
sha-automorphy-realization-exists-determ: UpperTheory.V.W.b0Ex (ProModularRingExists from PhiAll), through UpperTheory.V.CA.universalDeformationRing_nonempty_of_nonempty_pair, for the residual datum of a link: W.Resid with psib the restriction of chib, so that residual_ok_of_local_chars_restrict gives Resid.Ok and residual_diagonal_determinant_isPolar the pair over the residue field. The Lean states the existence for every residual datum with an ordinary pair over some complete local noetherian ring; the statement combines it with the residual pair, as cRealAv does. The finiteness conditions are PhiAll, from Pa.CohP (the published global and local finiteness); the text takes them from Lemma sha-patching-places. The ring R_0 is univDet_mf (Chenevier [Che14]), the R_{v,i} are universalDeformationRing_localCharacters and R_1 is coprod_opt (co_coprod). The proof follows the Lean.
sha-automorphy-realization-exists-linked: UpperTheory.V.Fr.space_ex, for a Frame with Ok C_0 and n in {2,3}: Nonempty (Fr.Space O F n). The universal lifting ring is Alg.univ_lift, Mazur's theorem [Maz89] for framed lifts, proved in the Lean from the finiteness of the lifts to the dual numbers. In (v), the Lean's tri_diag treats n = 2 and n = 3 by cases; the text gives the same computation for all n. The proof follows the Lean.
sha-automorphy-realization-seed: UpperTheory.V.Pr.seedPtOf_alt (Pr.SeedPtOf), with Sd.IsSeed for the seed and R.B_0.PT iota J for the property of automorphic points; the conclusion is Setup.IdealSpecializationPoint J (MatIrr of the linked point, J in the kernel, the determinant equation). A seed is Sd.IsSeedAlt iota sigma psi tau m kappa r: cont, irr (IsIrr, irreducible on the whole group), pair (a symmetric P with IsPair sigma r 1 P), res (ResSum: congruent characteristic polynomials), away (TypeAway: diagonal on inertia with the tau_i), above (OrdAt: a flag on D_A with characters equal to cyc^(m_i) on inertia and congruent to psi_i) and aut (IsAutCsdA for the twist), as the text lists them. The hypotheses on chi' (order prime to l, chi_cyc^j chi' congruent to Psi) are those of the seed datum, and GlobalArtinReciprocity is a hypothesis. The proof follows the Lean; step (8) is universalMaps_point_of_polarized_flagged_rep (Lemma sha-automorphy-realization-seed-point). The pair (rho', psi') of the conclusion is a Fr.NRep over the field K': conditions (a) to (c) of the definition of a linked point, without continuity or reduction. Its irreducibility is MatIrr top (0 and K'^n are the only stable subspaces), K' is an O_1-algebra, the map is an O_1-algebra map, and the determinant equation is T.B.u.D.map phi = W.GDet.ofRep (T.K.tw rho'), the determinant of g -> kappa_0(g) rho'(pi(g)), as the statement says.
sha-automorphy-realization-seed-normal: The private skew_eig and skew_norm of OfForm.lean, used in the proof of UpperTheory.V.Fr.of_form; J_n is Jmat K n and the e_{n,i} are Fr.w n i.
sha-automorphy-realization-seed-point: UpperTheory.universalMaps_point_of_polarized_flagged_rep, through the private main of the same file and UpperTheory.V.Fr.of_form. The hypotheses: r is IsIrr, Q is symmetric with the form identity, rho = tw (r.comp pi) kappa, T.B.u.Maps x for the determinant of rho and the characters, and HasFlag on each decomposition group. The conclusion is a Fr.NRep (conditions (a) to (c)) with MatIrr and the determinant equation. of_form also gives Integral (traces and characters in C with their reductions, and zeta), which this statement does not keep.
sha-automorphy-realization-ideal: UpperTheory.V.Pr.modularity_linked_ends: J with Setup.ModIn J (fin, dim = DimT, unr = Unr0 at v0, n4, p1 and p3 = P1core and P3core, seed) and R.B_0.arithmeticPointClassicalityDense iota J; the hypotheses are W.ModUAlt, W.LamEx and W.Large. The proof follows the Lean. ModUAlt is W.modU_of_printsH, from HidaUAlt (Proposition sha-hecke-ideal) and PfromAut (Proposition sha-patching-bound); LamEx is W.lamEx, from LocCFTAll (local class field theory). The condition at v0 used in step (3) is r.V0ok, the field v0 of CReal, which the text adds to the definition of a realization. The last sentence, (N4) for every arc, is the field n4 of Setup.ModIn.
sha-automorphy-realization-dimension: UpperTheory.V.Pr.dimOf (Pr.DimOf), through AnnihilatorQuotientFinite.component (the minimal prime contracts to 0, and the dimensions of an injective integral extension agree, GlobalTheory.ringKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral) and the dimension of a power series ring over a discrete valuation ring (GlobalTheory.FormalIsogeny.ringKrullDim_mvPowerSeries). Dimension is qdim, the Krull dimension of the quotient. The proof follows the Lean.
sha-automorphy-realization-arcs: UpperTheory.V.Pr.n4Of (Pr.EveryPointSatisfiesFrameCondition), proved by the private absolute_irreducible_rank_four of EveryPointSatisfiesFrameConditionAlt.lean from r.V0ok, through the private key (the invertibility of P(zA) modulo T). The Lean states it for the residual datum of a realization; its proof uses only the conditions at v0 in the statement. The proof follows the Lean.
sha-automorphy-realization-components: UpperTheory.V.Pr.absMain (Pr.AbsMain): (1) is Setup.GoodPt J_n for n = 2, 3 and (2) is FinPt O_1 Phi 3. (0) is UpperTheory.V.J.absGood (J.AbsGood), with the same hypotheses (Setup.ModIn J_2 and J_3): IsPhi, surjectivity onto S.B and AllGood S (J_3.map phi); it shares the first steps of absMain. B is S.B, and the off-triangular primes of AllGood are primes of S.A, the text's A_3^circ. In (1) and (2), A is any ring with IsCD O_1 A: a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field and a local map from O_1, not necessarily finite over O_1 (it may have characteristic l). The linked point satisfies IsLiftA (continuity, and modulo the maximal ideal the residual diagonal entries and characters and zero entries off the diagonal). In (1) the irreducibility is MatIrr top over some field K' with an injective j : A -> K', which amounts to irreducibility over the fraction field of A, not absolute irreducibility. In (2) A is also an algebra over the residue field k_1 of O_1 compatibly with O_1 (IsScalarTower), and the conclusion holds at every g in Gamma_0; FinPt says nothing about other complete local rings of characteristic l, and the only use, the finiteness (i) of Theorem sha-residually-reducible-automorphy through finEnd_of_finPt and finPtDown, is for such A. The proof follows absMain and absGood through Lemmas sha-automorphy-realization-components-transfer and sha-automorphy-realization-components-propagation, which are written out to the lemmas sha-automorphy-realization-components-transfer-twist to -local-point and sha-automorphy-realization-components-propagation-global to -diagonal; the open steps that remain are marked in those lemmas (and in the lemmas they cite).
sha-automorphy-realization-components-tr: For a Setup T (the realization) and Phi with T.IsPhi Phi and Phi surjective: (a) is UpperTheory.V.Pr.phiEx (Setup.PhiEx); (b) is finLamOf (FinLam: S.mB <= rad(J.map Phi + S.lamId)), from ModIn.fin; (c) is p1Of (P1'), from n4 and p1; (d) is rankThree_deformationSetup_splitting_condition (P23'), from n4 and p3; (e) is seedOf (SeedIn, qdim Z = 1 + n F.d), from unr, dim and seed; (f) is goodPtOf (AllGood -> GoodPt). A completion at x is Space.Loc x; off-triangular is NRep.TI, endoscopic NRep.TE, nice Pr.Nice (Coin over F.Nv v = I_v meet the kernel of the cyclotomic character), thick Fr.Thick (IsThickMod), thickly linked Pr.ThickLink, and P_B is L.pi P. The text writes phi(J_n) for the ideal J.map Phi, which is the image as Phi is surjective. The proof of (b) follows finLamOf, which is stated for every LamObj Lambda over which B_n / J is finite. The proofs of (a) and (c) to (f) follow phiEx, p1Of, rankThree_deformationSetup_splitting_condition, seedOf and goodPtOf down to the lemmas sha-automorphy-realization-components-transfer-twist to -local-point; those of -arc, -nice, -thick, -field-point and -untwist keep narrower open steps, and -local-point cites Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-near-completion-points. The notions of completion and of the kinds of primes are now Definition sha-automorphy-realization-components-transfer-primes.

Lambda_B is UpperTheory.V.Fr.Space.lamId and P_B is Space.Loc.pi P. A completion at x is Space.Loc x (the fields O', unr, R, iota, lies and univ). Off-triangular is NRep.TI, endoscopic NRep.TE, nice Pr.Nice (the fields prime, dim, char, off and sep, with Coin over F.Nv v, the elements of I_v at which the cyclotomic character is 1), thick Fr.Thick (TE and IsThickMod: even, sub, ord, ord_star and nonsplit, with continuous entries), and thickly linked Pr.ThickLink.

The private px_pair of PxIsCont.lean, a W.Pair r A for K : TwLink F r, A with IsCO O A, CharP (ResidueField O) l, n /= 0 and IsLift O rho. (1) is UpperTheory.V.CA.u_gen, for O local and R, R' with IsCO O. UpperTheory.V.Pr.pointEx (Setup.PointEx): for Phi with IsPhi, a completion L at x and a prime p of L.R with qdim p = 1 and l in p, there are y : W.Point T.r (an arc over PowerSeries K, K finite) and a local j : L.R -> y.A with kernel p, mat y.rho = K.tw (L.rho.map j), y.psi = K.twpsi (L.rho.map j) and B.IsPt y (j o phi). UpperTheory.V.Pr.T.curveNorm (CurveNorm.lean): for R a noetherian local domain, complete for its maximal ideal, with finite residue field, CharP R p and ringKrullDim R = 1, a finite field k and an injective, local and finite ring map R -> PowerSeries k. Step (1) is curveOverSeries and follows the Lean. Steps (2) and (3) are standard results that the Lean proves its own way: Serre's Proposition 3 of Chapter II, Section 2 (B a discrete valuation ring, free of rank [L:K] over A, L complete) is completeDVRExt, which gives only the finiteness of B and that B is a discrete valuation ring, the completeness of B being proved separately through R (curveDVR_complete); Serre's Theorem 2 of Chapter II, Section 4 (a complete discrete valuation ring of equal characteristic with perfect residue field is k[[T]]) is replaced by a coefficient field from the formal smoothness of the finite field over F_p (curveNorm_coeffField) and the isomorphism sending T to a uniformizer (exists_ringEquiv_powerSeries_of_complete).

UpperTheory.V.Fr.flag_loc (FlagLoc.lean): for a group H, a local ring C, r : H ->* Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) C, characters psi i : H ->* C^x and g_0 with the three hypotheses (the third as ordProd r psi g = 0 for all g), HasFlag r.toHomUnits psi: some g in GL_n(C) makes g r(s) g^-1 upper triangular with diagonal psi i s. sha-automorphy-unramified-near-completio: UpperTheory.V.Fr.loc_ex (a Space.Loc x exists when x is maximal and contains S.mB), UpperTheory.V.Fr.loc_flat (L.iota is flat), the first part of UpperTheory.V.Fr.loc_dim, and UpperTheory.V.Fr.pres (Loc.Pres, with N = N' + (n d + 1)). UpperTheory.V.Fr.flag, for any ring map f : S.A ->+* C to a local ring, with conclusion W.HasFlag ((S.u.map f).r.comp (F.loc0 v)).toHomUnits ((S.u.map f).psi v); the characteristic polynomial is UpperTheory.V.Fr.o1. The proof follows the Lean.

UpperTheory.V.Fr.point_loc, for C with UpperTheory.V.CA.IsCL O C (complete local, local structure map, residue field finite over that of O), a residue map f with IsResMap O C f, and an NRep rho over C with rho.Cont (maximalIdeal C) and (rho.map (residue C)).IsBar f; the conclusion S.x0 <= comap xi (maximalIdeal C), with S.x0 the ideal generated by S.mB, is the condition on the maximal ideal of B. UpperTheory.V.CA.cl_sub, for O local noetherian and adically complete and C with CA.IsCL O C; the subalgebra is the S of its conclusion, with IsCO O S (complete, local structure map, residue field that of O) and the comparison of the powers of the maximal ideals. (1) is the private tri_of_bar of PointLoc.lean, for an NRep over a field with IsBar f (only its diagonal part is used); (2) is the private cyc_mem, for an NRep over a local ring whose reduction satisfies IsBar f. The Lean treats n = 2 and n = 3 separately, as the text does.

The ring R is lauSub P of AlgDefs.lean and n is vertex h for h : HasVertex P (the hypotheses zero and cross); (2) is alg_homog, and (3) is the private alg_vring of AlgVring.lean (IsVertexRing: inj, comap, surj) with alg_sep for the intersection. UpperTheory.V.Fr.alg, for C with IsCO O C and K with C -> K injective; the hypotheses (i) to (iv) are the fields dg, cyc, fg and cont, and psi of Fr.Cone O C rho (psi through IsPsi: adic continuity and residues). UpperTheory.V.Fr.ext_A, with the condition on the maximal ideal of B as S.x0 <= comap. The proof follows the Lean.

UpperTheory.V.Fr.pr_correct, for O local and C', C with IsCO O; the lifts are a SetLift p B, mu satisfies IsSq O mu (the text's conditions on mu) and p . mu = 0, and (i), (ii) are D.om x = (dOne ad beta x).map mu and D.a v s = (a v s).map mu. (1) is UpperTheory.V.Fr.pr_good for an NRep over a field with IsBar (its conclusion NRep.Good and lieT nonzero with thetaLie fixed); (2) is pr_ofbox, for a Box with Box.Cont, whose conclusion is B.Of rho with rho.Cont; (3) is pr_norm, for m_C' * ker p = 0 and (rho.bar O).Good (the text keeps its fields two and zd, which are the ones used), with conclusion h, rho' with rho'.map p = rho, continuity, and the two matrix identities for conjBy h B'.r. UpperTheory.V.Fr.HasObs O' R H, for an IsCO O' R; the maps ker p -> k' are O'-linear.

sha-automorphy-unramified-near-dense: UpperTheory.V.J.denseOf, for B_0 noetherian, phi surjective, D a natural number and Gd a predicate on maps B_0 to Qbar l; the conclusion is J.DenseB for J.map phi when D = 1 + n d.
sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents: UpperTheory.V.J.TanA, proved as tanA from GC.Hypotheses₂ and Loc.LocalPublishedTheorems, the published Galois cohomology and local inputs of the literature hypothesis. The text follows tanA_of down to Z.J.unitOf (step (1), Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit, whose conclusion is Z.J.UnitAt) and Z.J.tan (steps (2) and (3); step (2) is Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-count). sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.unitOf, which proves the statement UnitOfP from Loc.LocalPublishedTheorems; its conclusion UnitAt (S.rho.map xi) v i' is the text's g, t and the UnitStep (u, beta). The Lean's indices are 0, 1, 2 and i' : Fin 2 with castSucc and succ. The equality j = i + 1 is idxStep, which also gives k = 1. The published inputs are the hypotheses LocalFiniteness, LocalTateDuality, LocalEulerChar and BlochKatoLocal (dimension formula, rational and integral duality of Bloch and Kato); the Lean assumes them and proves the unit step from them (stepF, cupUnr, clearDen). Of these, the unit step uses only the rational duality of Bloch and Kato (Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-duality), in cupUnr; the facts on crystalline representations (restriction, coefficients, subquotients, twists, extensions of the trivial representation, unramified classes) are proved in the Lean, in PadicHodgeTheory, and the text follows these proofs in Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-crystalline.
sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-: Collects the Lean's facts on crystalline representations used by unitOf and cupUnr. The Lean's notion is UpperTheory.V.Loc.IsCr phi rho: finrank over Q_l of Dcr phi rho, the invariants in V (x) Bcr l with Bcr l = (PP l).R.B, equals (phi.range sup Iq l).index times finrank over Q_l of V; for phi the inclusion of G_K this index is [K_0 : Q_l] (isCrIff, sup_Iq), and IsCrys of Formalism.WeaklyAdmissibleFiltrations is the same condition with dimensions over the coefficient field (isCrField). (1) is GlobalTheory.Per.FontaineBound.finite_finrank_le_base; (2) is UpperTheory.V.Loc.isCrys_isDR_sub_quot (which also treats de Rham representations); (3) is the crystalline half of GlobalTheory.Per.TiedRestrict.restrict_crys_deRham; (4) is GlobalTheory.Pst.isCrys_ext_iff; (5) is the private isCr_inv and isCr_twist of MatrixExtendByZeroApply.lean; (6) is UpperTheory.V.Loc.crUnr; (7) is the private line of MatrixExtendByZeroApply.lean, used through UpperTheory.V.Loc.crExt. The properties of B_cris used in the proof are derived, as in the Lean, from the facts of Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-crystalline-periods, which the Lean proves for its own construction of the period rings (PP l with LocTied): the domain property is isDomain_cris, regularity is tied_frac_invariant and RegularRing.fracInv, and units on lines is RegularRing.lineUnit. Parts (5) to (7) follow the Lean: the criterion (c) is RegularRing.isCrys_iff_span, (d) is admissible_of_bilinear_openSubgroup_galois, (e) is isCrys_isDR_internalHom, (6) is the private isCrys_of_inertia through exists_witt_matrix (Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-crystalline-lang) and isCrys_of_split, and (7) is the private line. The Lean's proofs of (c) to (e) are its own versions of the formalism of regular rings in [BC09, Theorem 5.2.1].

Published facts of Fontaine's theory, stated as in [BC09]: (1) is Definition 4.4.7, Lemma 4.4.10 and Theorem 4.4.13; (2) is Definition 9.1.4 and the claim after it; (3) is Theorem 9.1.5; (4) is Proposition 9.1.6; (5) is (4.4.1) with Definition 9.1.4; (6) is the computation of g(t) in Section 4.4 with Proposition 9.1.3 and Definition 9.1.4. The Lean does not assume them: it constructs the rings (Per.Ainf, Per.Acris, Per.Bcris, Per.BdR, and the period datum PP l with AIP l and tiedP from GlobalTheory.MemLoc.exists_locPrime_tied) and proves each fact for its construction. (1) is isField_of_tied, the field invdR of Formalism.WeaklyAdmissibleFiltrations.PeriodData and the map C.oD of Qbar_l into B_dR; (2) is the fields actB and invB of PeriodData; (3) is used in the stronger-looking form Core.TensorInj (elements of Qbar_l linearly independent over Q_l^ur stay linearly independent over B_cris in B_dR), proved as GlobalTheory.T.algClosure_tensor_bcris_to_bdR_injective, which follows from (3) for a finite extension containing the elements; (4) is Core.Regular, proved as GlobalTheory.T.bcris_regular_of_tensorInj; (5) is the fields iA, ιA_inj and ιA_act of Formalism.BasicNotions.LocAinf with ιA_zlW; (6) is the fields t, t_unit and t_act of PeriodData.

GlobalTheory.UnramifiedCrys.eventually_actT_eq for (1) and GlobalTheory.UnramifiedCrys.norm_sub_lt_one_of_fix for (2), stated there for the whole group Gal(Qbar_l/Q_l) acting on the tilt OCb l through the field actT of LocAinf; (2) concludes that |g(x) - x| < 1 for every integer x of Qbar_l, and the Lean's inertia group IK K is the subgroup generated by such g (UpperTheory.V.Loc.memIK identifies it with the elements fixing Q_l^ur). The proof follows the Lean.

GlobalTheory.UnramifiedRep.exists_witt_matrix, for a group G with a homomorphism to the ring automorphisms of R and the openness hypothesis stated pointwise (hopen); M is a monoid homomorphism to the r x r matrices over Z_l, and the hypothesis on M is hJ. The proof follows the Lean. Step (c) is GlobalTheory.T.exists_unit_matrix_coboundary_of_fixed_frobenius_pow, Hilbert's Theorem 90 for GL_r [Ser79, Chapter X, Proposition 3], which the Lean proves by Serre's argument (UnramifiedHilbertNinety.exists_matrix_coboundary) for a cocycle with entries in F_m fixed by G; step (d) is exists_witt_trace_one, (e) is InvariantLift.average_step and (f) is InvariantLift.exists_invariant_lift.

GlobalTheory.Published.BlochKato.RationalDuality, the second field of GlobalTheory.Published.BlochKatoLocal, which the Lean assumes through the field bk of UpperTheory.V.Loc.LocalPublishedTheorems. Crystalline cocycles are Formalism.WeaklyAdmissibleFiltrations.finiteCocycles PD rho (a(g) (x) 1 = g x - x in V (x) B_cris), the pairing is IsDual1 (perfect, equivariant up to the cyclotomic character), and the coboundary condition is CobL PD (cupL rho' P a b). Bloch and Kato [BK90, Proposition 3.8] state that H^1_f(K,V) and H^1_f(K,V^*(1)) are exact annihilators of each other for V de Rham, with H^1_f defined in (3.7.2); this is the same statement, with V' and P in place of V^*(1). The unit step uses (1) from left to right.

UpperTheory.V.Z.J.cupUnr, for a group G with an open embedding into Gal(Qbar_l/Q_l), which openField identifies with G_K, and kappa in UpperTheory.V.Loc.finiteCocycles of chRep of the cyclotomic character with values in E. The proof follows the Lean; its step (3), that unramified homomorphisms are crystalline cocycles, is z1fUnr (rat_case), which the text follows through parts (6) and (7) of Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-unit-crystalline.
sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-count: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.tan up to its call of rankTwo: box_pt, box_unit, selLow and derOf with zn_ext. Its hypotheses are F.Ok C_0 (the residual conditions), l != 0, the complex conjugations cw, GWL (the Greenberg-Wiles formula, from GC.Hypotheses₂ through gwlOf) and LocE (the local Euler characteristic formulas, through leOf2); Z.J.tan concludes the two independent tangent vectors, and the text splits off the count before rankTwo. In tanA_of these hypotheses come from the realization (R.ok, R.T.lne) and from linkOf, gwlOf and leOf2 (Lemma sha-automorphy-unramified-tangents-count-inputs). The proof follows the Lean; Z_k is ZN B k and the injection is the map z to the derivation chosen by derOf.

(1) is UpperTheory.V.Z.J.LocE, that is LE l (F.Gv v) (F.eps.comp (F.loc v)) (F.dv v) for every v; (2) is UpperTheory.V.Z.J.GWL for the frame with cw replaced by the family (c'_w). Z^1(D,N) is Zc rho (locally constant cocycles), Hom_eps(N, Z/l^k) is HomMu l k eps rho (with eps reduced by PadicInt.toZModPow k), and Z_L is ZL F rho Z. The Lean states both for finite abelian groups N killed by l^k with a Z-linear action whose kernel is open, as the text does.

The hypotheses GWL and LocE of UpperTheory.V.Z.J.tan, as supplied in UpperTheory.V.J.tanA_of: linkOf gives the complex conjugations cw (with cw w * cw w = 1 and F.del (cw w) = -1) and the data GC.FLink; gwlOf and leOf2 derive GWL and LocE from GC.Hypotheses₂, whose fields gw, lf, lt and le are the published Greenberg-Wiles formula, local finiteness, local Tate duality and the local Euler characteristic formula, for finite modules over Z/l^r (Lemmas sha-descent-link-local-tate and sha-descent-link-greenberg-wiles, used with r = k), and gwlOf also uses the field gf (GlobalFiniteness) through the finiteness in Lemma sha-descent-link-greenberg-wiles. Relation to the literature: the same as classical results. Since chi is primitive modulo N, the cusp forms of level N with character chi contain no old forms, so g is a primitive form. (1) follows from the adjointness of T_p and conj(chi(p)) T_p for the Petersson product when p does not divide N, proved in [Miy89, Section 4.5], on the Hecke operators of S_k(N, chi) and their adjoints for the Petersson product: a_p <g,g> = <T_p g, g> = <g, conj(chi(p)) T_p g> = chi(p) conj(a_p) <g,g>. (2) is the first case of [Miy89, Theorem 4.6.17]: for a primitive form f in S_k(N, chi) and a prime p dividing N, if p has the same exponent in N and in the conductor of chi, then |a_p(f)| = p^((k-1)/2); here chi is primitive modulo N, so this holds at every p dividing N. (The theorem also gives a_p(f)^2 = chi_0(p) p^(k-2) when p exactly divides N and not the conductor, and a_p(f) = 0 otherwise.) Both citations were checked against published sources that quote Miyake with these numbers, from the 2006 reprint, which keeps the numbering of the 1989 edition; Miyake's text itself was not consulted.

Relation to the literature: the existence of kappa is of the kind of [CHT08, Lemma 4.1.4], which, for an algebraic character chi of the ideles of the totally real field with chi_v(-1) independent of the real place v, gives an algebraic character psi of the CM field with psi o N = chi o N and prescribed infinity type; the statement here is on the Galois side, for any continuous nu trivial on the complex conjugations, with no algebraicity, and it bounds the ramification of kappa outside Phi; the Lean does not cite [CHT08]. (5) is GC.phi, which is phiGam. (2) is GC.H2_unramified_inflation, stated for any profinite group with a closed normal subgroup I, a closed normal subgroup J of I of index prime to l on which the action is trivial, an element phi such that I and phi generate a dense subgroup, and homomorphisms onto every Z/n trivial on I and taking phi to 1; it is used for decomposition groups. The Lean proves (2) by an explicit construction of the cochain (Alg.exists_locallyConstant_dOne_eq_cocycle_of_tame_inertia); the text cites the published fact that D/N has l-cohomological dimension at most 1.

The proof follows the Lean. The statement is Tate's global Euler characteristic formula and the end of the Poitou-Tate sequence [NSW08, Chapter VIII, sections 6 and 7] for these modules.
sha-descent-link-global-tate: The hypotheses ReciprocityTheory.Gal.GlobalFiniteness, ReciprocityTheory.Gal.GlobalEulerChar and GlobalTheory.Published.PoitouTateNormalised (fields of the bundles of published Galois cohomology, for instance gf, ge and pt of Pa.CohP), quantified over every number field F with algebraic closure Omega, prime l, r, finite set S of finite places, and finite Z/l^r-module M with the discrete topology and a Representation of GS Omega S, the quotient of G_F by the closed normal subgroup NS generated by the inertia groups at the places outside S. (1) is GlobalFinitenessAt, under 0 < r, ContainsAbove S l and ContAction: Finite H0, H1 and H2, and Subsingleton (Hn n) for n >= 3 when l != 2. (2) is GlobalEulerCharAt, for a family c of elements of G_F indexed by the infinite places with IsCCAt at the real ones; archH0Card is the product over the real places of the fixed points of the c_w, times |M|^r_2. (3) is PoitouTateNormalised, under (l != 2 or F totally complex), 0 < r and a primitive l^r-th root of unity zeta: an InvFam inv such that inv A is bijective and IsNormalised zeta A v (part (a)) for every A over a finite place v, and, for every S containing the places above l (ContainsAbove), places Av over the v in S, a character mu of GS lifting cycMod (the text's chi_r; it is unique, as G_F -> GS is onto) and M with ContAction: NineTermExact (part (b), the maps tr0, tr1 and tr2 being built from cupH0H2TwistedDual, the flip of cupH1H1TwistedDual, cup20 and invAt), ShaDual and Subsingleton (Hn n) for n >= 3 (part (c)). The Lean's H1 x H1 cup product takes the dual class first; this changes tr1 by a sign and not the exactness. ShaDual also states the equalities of cardinalities that follow from the isomorphisms. The same as Tate's global finiteness and Euler characteristic theorems and the Poitou-Tate exact sequence and duality [NSW08, Chapter VIII, sections 6 and 7] for finite modules of l-power order, with the local invariants normalised by the cup product of a Kummer class of a uniformiser with the unramified character taking Frobenius to 1. The Lean states it for every r; the uses in Chapter 10 are the case r = 1.
sha-descent-link-greenberg-wiles: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.GreenbergWiles, the field gw of GC.Hypotheses2: GreenbergWilesAt for finite Z/l^r-modules M over GS with r > 0 and l odd, a character mu of GS lifting cycMod, local conditions LocCond, and perpCond, their annihilators under cupH1H1TwistedDual. The statement is the Lean's, for any r >= 1; the uses in Chapter 10 over F_l-vector spaces are the case r = 1. It is stated with cardinalities (Nat.card); the factor archH0Card is the product over the real places of the fixed points of the c_w times |M|^r_2. The finiteness of H^1 is not part of GreenbergWilesAt: it is GlobalFiniteness. sha-descent-link-hermite: Kum.finChar, for a primitive n-th root of unity in E. sha-descent-link-hilbert: Kum.artKer: the kernel of Kum.artCl, the restriction to the Hilbert class field followed by the inverse of GroundTheory.Global.hilbertClassFieldArtinEquiv, lies in the kernel of chi. sha-descent-link-cone: GC.coneCount, stated for surjections q_v from W onto spaces Q_v, with b_v = ker q_v, and for the groups coneH0, Fr.H1C and Fr.coneH2 of locally constant cochains. sha-hecke-situation: W.HidaSetting gives the places: St are the auxiliary places, v0 has normV v0 = p for an odd prime p not l and unramified in L, and HidaSetting.unr is the condition that L/L^+ be unramified at the finite places. The Lean's UniversalOrdinaryDeterminantRing.IsStable is instead absolute irreducibility (U3.MatIrr on the whole group over the algebraic closure kap q); Det.stableIff shows the two agree (Remark sha-patching-chain-burnside), and IsStable is the form in the statements P1core and P3core. sha-hecke-data: Hi.nonempty_unitaryHeckeData builds Hi.CaseU.UnitaryHeckeData from exists_integral_type_for_residual_rep (TypeForAlt), exists_theta_is_weight_of_lam_obj (IsTheta and IsWt, where the freeness condition Frame.Free holds by neatU) and exists_is_res_of_residual_rep_and_type (IsRes). Iwa.uOp is U_alpha, a finite sum over N/(Nconj a); Iwa.eig is V(c, phi), on which t acts by phi(t)^{-1}; invPart is the ordinary part. sha-hecke-local-principal: Hi.exists_principal_series_of_distinct_inv_ne_bot, from the literature hypothesis (LitLocAlt: Bernstein-Zelevinsky finiteness and the geometric lemma). Its steps: OrdB.inv_inj (the Jacquet projection is injective on the ordinary part, by the Fitting decomposition of U_z on the finite-dimensional V(c, phi) and propCker), OrdB.exists_form, GlobalTheory.SatakeExists.isSubquotient_of_eigenform (Frobenius reciprocity), AlgebraTools.jqMult (multiplicities in the Jacquet module of a principal series, from the geometric lemma), OrdB.le_gen, prin_series_irreducible_and_unique_subquotient, and propCp with hidx and OrdB.num for the eigenvalues. sha-hecke-local-rec: Hi.psRec_s_ty, proved by Z.Win.T2.psRec_alt: the local Artin map of IsRecT is a (GlobalTheory.ArtinLocalInj.artin_localIdele_injective, with ChevalleyUnits), then hasSupport_iff (the laws through LawsV.supp, cusp, one and inj, with ZelevinskyPolynomialRing), hasSupport_of_isSubquotient_prinSeries, isSubquotient_of_hasSupport and the twist SupportRing.hasSupport_nu. The maps rc are those with IsRecT, which the book calls maps satisfying the laws.
sha-hecke-local-global: The hypothesis is the part above l of Z.Win.LocGlobT, that is CmpT: for every rc with IsRecT such that y = rc(algNorm sigma) satisfies Gd (abelian and mono0), the restriction is potentially semistable (IsPstAt) with wdAt equal to y; together with Z.Desc.P.HtGT for the Hodge-Tate weights (IsdRAt and IsJumpsAt, asserted when the local component is PlainTor). The formula eps(s) = q^{d(s)} prod tau(a(s)) is Loc.epsArt, proved from global reciprocity; the reduction to units and one uniformizer is eig_gen, and the induction on i is eig_tele.
sha-hecke-local-flag: Hi.OrdFlag, proved by Loc.ordFlag_alt from the literature hypothesis (Berger's theorem DeRhamPotSemistable). The relation for the psi_j is OrdChar. The induction is the private lemma flag: ordChar_inv; the twist twR with deRham_rational_twist_by_character and V.Loc.hecke_char_de_rham_of_local_artin_above_l; the private lemma core for the invariant vector (core0, with inertia_eigenvector_extends_of_distinct_characters for N = 0 and the eigenline, and exists_invariant_vector_of_finite_image_averaging and exists_frobenius_fixed_period for the phi-fixed period; then exists_invariant_of_dpst_phi_fixed_of_nonneg_weights); exists_common_eigenline, deRhamRational_of_conj and deRham_rational_of_extension_by_character. (1) is exists_automorphicForm_with_prescribed_iwahori_values and (2) is mem_lattice_of_values_at_double_coset_reps, both for representatives x : Fin N -> Ga x Gp of the double cosets of U x Iw c, which the Lean takes from exists_finite_iwahori_doubleCoset_representatives (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-sections (1)); (2) does not use the disjointness or the freeness. exists_integral_form_lifting_controlMap: for F in ClO W tau U c phi and Lat (mIm O Omega 0), an f in Frame.Sp tau theta U (the book's F_{O'}(U, theta')) with mapFn f = ctrl F, and the congruence on Nm c' for c' at least c whenever W.xi is congruent to 1 modulo the k-th power of the maximal ideal on Nm c'.

(1) is ordExists (IsOrdProj for ordProj I U, its range ordPart U, which is the book's P, the intersection of the ranges of the U^n, and the bijectivity of U on it), (2) is ordFactLim (IsFactLim for ordProj), (3) is ordProjective with Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing and ordPer, and (4) is span_ordinaryPart_eq_sup_unit_generalized_eigenspaces with eigOrdInt; all in the Lean's HidaCompleteRings library for a complete local ring with finite residue field (OrdAdm). The proofs follow the Lean: (1) through ordLimProj and ordLimBij, with the projectors modulo the powers of m from ordFinLen and made compatible by ordNatLin, and (2) through ordFactFin and ordNatLin. The Lean's ordExists is stated for ordProj m U, a chosen ordinary projector, which is one because the limit e is; the book's (1) states the existence of e, and its proof of (2) works for any ordinary projector. ordFactLim is an equivalence, IsFactLim m U e if and only if e = ordProj m U; the book states the direction used.
IsOrdProj I U e, a structure with the fields idem, comm, bij (Set.BijOn U on range e) and nil (for every k an n with U^n (x - e x) in I^k M for all x).

(1) is ordCancel; (2) is ordNatLin, the R-linear case of ordNat, which allows two rings and a map f continuous for the adic topologies; (3) is the first conjunct of ordRange (range e = ordPart U), whose other conjuncts, ker e = nilPart I U and the complement, are not stated.

ordFinLen, for IsFiniteLength R M. The Lean takes Fitting's decomposition from Mathlib (LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow: the kernel and the range of U^k are complementary for all large k) and the stabilization of the ranges from LinearMap.eventually_iInf_range_pow_eq; the book cites Fitting's lemma [Jac09, pp. 113-114], which gives the decomposition M = U^infinity(M) + U^-infinity(0) of a noetherian and artinian module, the form of Mathlib's statement for k beyond the stabilization of the kernels and ranges. The proof then follows ordFinLen with N = n + m.
factIdem, for a finite monoid, and ordFactFin, for a module with [Finite M]; the book combines them. factIdem also gives that U^(N!) is idempotent, which is part of the ordinary projector.

exists_free_lattice_spanning_ordinary_part, with C, T and ev as in the book and the sum over the mu with IsIntUnit O mu. The book's S is (ordPart T0).map L, with L the composite of the inclusion of O^iota and the inverse g of ev on C.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-contro: Sp.absSpec (FreeMap.lean), for a Frame X, a family U : Lambda -> Subgroup X.Ub with hdir, hfin (FinLevel) and hfree (Frame.Free), a WtRep W over a complete local domain O with Function.Injective (algebraMap O Omega) and algebraMap A O local, phi trivial on Tc c with c at least W.c0, and hchi. (1) is its first conjunct; (2) is its second: add, smul, span (with Frame.ClOrd at every e at least c), indep, the U operators at the a in I.P with UF, and the finite sums of raF between U K and U K'. The proof follows the Lean: Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-classical is hCF and the integrality of the sums, Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-inputs (2) is hCO, Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-base-change is hBC, and sp is defined through the predicate Good and its uniqueness.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-decomp: The two conjuncts of Hi.clParts_alt, which the Lean states for every e at least c0 under HSet.Ax, IsWt, AutomorphicHeckeSet P and IsSpec, using of IsSpec only fin (the finite dimension) and triv (phi trivial on T_0^(c0)); the book states it for a weight datum and phi trivial on T_0^(c), with the finite dimension from Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-classical and AutomorphicHeckeSet from Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-inputs (3). The Lean sums over the parts satisfying P; the sum over all parts is then the same. The proof follows classical_in_iwahori_parts (cl_avg with cl_proj, cl_multi, cl_iso, cl_back with mem_fixd_lev and cl_KO) and cl_gen.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-hida-eigen: The private pa_fin of HeckeOperatorPreservesPart.lean, which partAct0_alt applies with Y0 = Ord (lev K), Y = HSet.MK, e from locIdem, chi = iota x and the fields add, smul, indep and op of IsSpec. In the Lean, (3) is stated for O-algebra maps y with iota y = z (pa_pt); its fourth conclusion, an eigenvector in some Z_j meet O for every character of T_Y equal to chi on A, is not stated. The proof follows pa_rho, pa_op, pa_stab, pa_inst (hfix, hin, hsum) and pa_chr.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-torsion: The private nt_free of NtExpand.lean, for the principal congruence subgroup Kc of level 1 at a place w over p, with p odd and not dividing the discriminant of L. The proof follows nt_sq, nt_mat (induction on primes), nt_prime and nt_step.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-finite-orde: The private nt_ord of NtExpand.lean, with a map T choosing a place of L above each finite place of L^+; its unitarity hypothesis is stated for every power M^k, which follows from the case k = 1. The proof follows nt_char, nt_int and nt_fin.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-uop: (1) is Hi.uOpMul, stated for any Iwa structure, here the product over the factors (piIwa of glIwa); its last clause, U_a v = pi(a) v when a^-1 is also in P, is not stated. (2) and (3) are the first two conjuncts of Hi.uOpLevel; its statements on the eigenspaces Iwa.eig are not stated. In glIwa, Tc c is the diagonal torus congruent to 1 modulo varpi^(c+1), Nm c is Nbar_c, Iwa.I1 c is generated by N0, Tc c and Nm c, and P is the monoid of dominant diagonal matrices diag(varpi^(a_i)). The proofs follow uOpMul_sum, uOpMul_ex and uOpLevel_core.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-forms: (1) is the first four conjuncts of Hi.spStab (Frame.Amb stable under U_a and under ra, U_a commuting with ra, Sp U and Ord U stable under U_a); its last conjunct, on double coset operators between two subgroups, is not stated. (2) is exists_adic_limit_mem_automorphicSpace and (3) is uOperator_pow_eventually_invariant_mod_pow. The Lean works with the reduction modulo m^k through Frame.mapFn and uOpNat.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-sections: (1) is exists_finite_iwahori_doubleCoset_representatives, (2) is exists_section_automorphicSpace_with_prescribed_values (through exists_iwahori_torus_projection and exists_linear_section_automorphicFunctions_of_free) and (3) is mem_valIn_of_invariant_and_values_mem_pow. The freeness condition is Frame.Free; I(c) is Iwa.Iw c = N0 T0 Nbar_c. The Lean's representatives are indexed by Fin N, with the uniqueness of the index stated separately.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-projector: Hi.ordAbs, with exists_ordinaryProjector_of_eventually_periodic and exists_linear_preimage_of_successive_approximation for two of its steps. The Lean takes O as a submodule characterized by the condition of the statement, with T^(n+1) in place of T^n for n at least 1. The proof follows the Lean step by step.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-ordinary: Hi.ordStruct, for a subgroup U with Frame.FinLevel and Frame.Free; (1) is its first three conjuncts, (2) is the conjunct hfilt and (3) is the map e, defined on Sp U, the book's F(U). Hi.ordFree adds that U_a is bijective on Ord U for every dominant a, which is not stated here. The proof follows ordStruct: the hypotheses of ordAbs come from spStab, exists_adic_limit_mem_automorphicSpace and the three statements of Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-sections, and mem_ord_iff identifies O with Ord U.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-spherical: The first two conjuncts of Hi.sphComm (its third, on sphOp at 0 and n, is not stated), with Hi.dcGelfand for the commutation. This is the commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra of GL_n, which the Lean proves by Gelfand's argument with the transpose (s x = invT (x^-1)) and the Smith normal form (sphC_cartan); the book follows the Lean's proof. The Lean states it for the double coset operators dc rho K K x on K-fixed vectors of any representation over a commutative ring.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-projective: Hi.ordProj, with its three conjuncts: the projectivity over the group ring; the image of Ord V under the double coset operator dc (ra tau) U V 1, which on V-fixed vectors is the trace (ordProj_dc); and the elements of Ord V in the kernel of that operator. The Lean's hypotheses are V normal in U (as subgroupOf), of finite relative index, U of finite level and neat, and theta continuous; it derives the freeness condition Frame.Free of U from neatness (hFU), the finite level and freeness condition of V with Ord U = Ord V meet the U-fixed vectors (ordLevel), the freeness of Ord V (ordFree) and e_V (ordStruct), and the book does the same. Only (1) is used in the book. The proof follows ordProj_ord, ordProj_chi, ordProj_mul, ordProj_phi, ordProj_higman (Higman's criterion), htrinv, htrinvL and hsumw.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-sum: Hi.piBasic, through the private pb_main. Its conclusions: rho with rho (single q g) = ra (sec (w_q) g); the vectors fixed by pi K mapped onto MK; every element in some MK; and, given the neatness of all levels and the faithfulness condition on the sections (supplied by neatU and levelUR2Faith in s3), the projectivity of the vectors fixed by pi K' over the group ring of the quotient. For the book's product levels the faithfulness condition holds by definition. The monotonicity in (1) is hMle in pb_main and the mono of piPts_dir.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-unique: Hi.levelUR2BaseEq_alt, for the change of level V -> V0, with p the level-change map p0 h and phi an A-algebra map sending gen i to gen (j i); Hi.core_unique_of_axioms_weight_char is the case of one level with phi the identity, and the private lc_univ of LevelUR2Compat.lean transports IsUniv along a Hecke map. The density of the inverse Frobenius elements is the field dense of HSet.Ax and the surjectivity of the Artin map is art_spec; the determinant is recovered from its coefficients at group elements by CA.d_gext.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-compatible: Hi.level_change_compat_rank_two_of_dense_weight, with levelUR2HeckeMap for Phi; the Lean states the hypothesis on phi for the generators of TK. The uniqueness of maps out of B' is base_object_hom_ext, which s3 passes as hU.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-action: Hi.levelUR2ActEx_alt. Its hypothesis hJ, an ideal with IsJ at every K, comes from Hi.exists_hecke_ideal at the augmented level through LvW.step1_alt, which the book cites as the proof of Proposition sha-hecke-ideal for S'. The gluing is levelUR2Glue.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-eigensystem: Hi.levelUR2OrdPt_alt, at a point x with IsSpec, which spec supplies at every x with HSet.Arith, the book's arithmetic points of Lambda; admitted is Set.univ. The first paragraph follows the private op_eig (AnnihilatorQuotientFinite.pointEig: fibreNe and eigOfQuot), the second levelUR2EigPart.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-base: (1) is LvW.step2_alt, that is levelUR2LocEq_alt: levelUR2LevEq for the levels, the equality of the operators through opUp, and levelUR2H3Abs_alt for the localizations, with levelUR2LocSub (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-fewer), levelUR2OrdPt_alt for the HSet at V0 (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-eigensystems for S), levelUR2GalRes and the private hecke_part_frobenius. (2) is levelUR2SmulKey_alt, with sk_hecke, levelUR2BaseEq_alt (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-unique) and sk_comp; s3 combines it with eq_sub to give e0.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-points: Hi.piPts_n_alt, followed step by step: piPts_dir, spec and piPts_coord for sp(z) nonzero; partAct0_alt and the first conjunct of core_eigen_of_weight_char_hecke_level at the levels containing z; the private piPts_abs (PiLin.exists_desc, PiLin.exists_proj); isoRefine with isoPick and isoSub; piPts_conj (AlgebraTools.Det.bnRep and woConj'_alt). The Lean's alpha is any ring map with, at each K, a map to TK and characters satisfying IsUniv; the book uses the alpha of Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-augmented-action, which umodAbs_alt passes.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-base: Pa.TWBase u J Empty D, with wt : WtVars (v, i, gamma, c) and wt_res. The Lean takes gamma_k in the decomposition group Gv; the construction in the proof of (7) takes it in inertia. M carries its own module structure over abelian2 O Empty D = O[[X_1, ..., X_D]], with smul_lam (a acts as lam a), Module.Free and Module.Finite over it, and supp: for every prime p of B, the annihilator of M is in p if and only if J is.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-iwahori: AlgebraTools.iwC k n C is the supremum of KOne (congruent to 1 modulo the maximal ideal), unipO (upper unipotent with integral entries) and the image under diagT of torC C (diagonal units with residues in C). Pa.ellC l is the subgroup of elements of order prime to l. Dom t says valuation (t i) <= valuation (t j) for i <= j, for the multiplicative valuation. Hi.dc is the finsum over the orbit of K on G/K' through x, with representatives given by out; AlgebraTools.hk2 restricts it to the fixed vectors, and is 0 when the image is not contained in the K-fixed vectors.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-torus: Pa.Lev.thetaQ gives Theta with IsThetaQ rho C Theta: Theta_j(t) is Hi.dc of rho composed with the j-th factor at diagT t for Dom t, and the Theta_j(t) commute. The uniqueness is AlgebraTools.thetaEx (an existence and uniqueness statement) for one factor. Both assume that resCard is a unit in A.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-diamond: (1) is Pa.Lev.delIso, with Del l n a for a_j = padicValNat l (qj w j - 1); the normality of UIw1 in UIw is an instance hypothesis there, supplied by levelUR2IwLev in the construction of the level module. (2) is Pa.Lev.trOf for a ThData T: act1 (1 + y_{j,i}) is the action of diagT (e_i(delta_j)), the norm map is hk2 rho UIw UIw1 1, and it commutes with act1 u_{j,i} and actw u_{j,i}; the commutation for all t is the private trOf_main.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-dimension: AlgebraTools.jqLine, from the published hypotheses GeometricLemma and BernsteinZelevinskyFiniteness (fields of Pa.LocPAlt). It also bounds by 1 the dimension of a common generalized eigenspace when the characters psi_i are distinct, which is not used here. The book cites Borel and Casselman, and Bernstein and Zelevinsky, for the bound.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-local: Z.Win.LocDataTAlt, proved by Z.Win.locDataT_alt from Pa.LocPAlt (BernsteinZelevinskyFiniteness, GeometricLemma and TameLocal); the conclusion is LocRelT l x delta sigma (iota r(fr)) (iota r(tau)), together with resCard = normV w. The hypothesis on sigma is WDT iota r (rc (algNorm sigma)) for every rc with IsRecT: a Weil-Deligne representation of r exists (IsWDOf) and equals rc(sigma nu^((1-n)/2)) when the latter satisfies Gd (abelian and monodromy-free). The Lean's r is any group homomorphism. The eigenvalues are resCard^i chi(Pi.mulSingle i x) with i from 0, which is q_w^(i-1) chi(e_i(x)) with i from 1.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-level-module: (1) is Pa.LevMod b h w: rN with Glob.Compat h rN (residOf r) (the characters chib composed with p, the same psib and th), the pair p, the algebra structure over abelian2 O Empty D with segmentWeightExponent, beta with beta_pair, P with rho, fin (finite over Lambda on the UIw1-fixed vectors), proj (normality and projectivity over the group ring of UIw/UIw1), eM and eM_smul. The Lean's level is any V : s.Lev with h : (globOf r V).Hom (globOf r V0); the book takes the Galois group of the maximal extension unramified outside a finite set S' containing S. (2) is Pa.LevPtAlt, whose field lg is WOT iota (rep composed with V.pr) (rc (algNorm (sigma j))) for every valuation ring Bq over w_j and every rc with IsRecT; WOT is WDT. (3) is LevMod.ClassicalAlt, which also quantifies over iota. (4) is Pa.Lev.LocalLevelConditions, whose second field is LocRelT for every point and every j.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-kill: Pa.Lev.relOf_alt, for F in MvPolynomial (Fin n + Fin n) R renamed into the variables of index j, with T : ThData. It assumes Pa.LocPAlt, w_j not above l, IsUnif x_j and IsGenMod delta_j; the last three are not used in its proof, and the book keeps them in the statement, marked as unused. It quantifies over the theta with IsTheta for sigma_{y,j} and ellC. The local step is Pa.Lev.nilKill (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-nil).
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-operator-module: (1) is Pa.Lev.OpMod b h q N: M1 with act1 from PUY R q n (the variables uV and yV are U_{j,i} and Y_{j,i}), Mw with actw from PU R q n, rho : Representation Lambda (Del l n a) M1 with rho_gen and proj, and tr with tr_surj, tr_ker and tr_u. (2) is Pa.Lev.OpRel A Nq ph ta ex: two is TwoMaps with MSplitAlg, the universal splitting algebra of the polynomials u.D.chi (single (h.p0 (ph j)) 1), and f = fEl Nq of the variables; rel1 and rel2 are act1 of the ex-th powers of fEl Nq (uV) times the trace of A.p.D mapped to PUY at single g 1 * q1El and single g 1 * q2El. The integers b_j are Nq.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-comparison: Pa.Lev.twoOf_alt, for a ThData T built by thEx, giving TwoMaps for T.actw; it assumes Pa.LocPAlt, w_j not above l (used by the private unit_card: q_(w_j) is a unit in O), IsUnif x_j, IsGenMod delta_j (not used) and LocalLevelConditions. The proof is the private two_gen applied to the e_j of Pa.Lev.hkHypOf (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-trace with the commutation and stability steps), to Z.Win.T2.symOf_alt (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-symmetric) and to the eM of the level module, through multiTwo and twoMul (Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-tw-split).
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-operators: Pa.Lev.opOf_alt, which assumes Pa.LocPAlt, w_j not above l, IsUnif x_j, IsGenMod delta_j, LocalLevelConditions A x delta ph ta and qj w j = 1 modulo l^N, and returns an OpMod with the ring data of A, M1 = fixd A.rho (UC n w ellC), Mw = fixd A.rho (UC n w top) and a_j = padicValNat l (qj w j - 1), with OpRel for ex = n!. The relations are Z.Win.T2.level_relation_one_two.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-nilpotent: Pa.Lev.OpP.nilPart returns an abstract module N with Lambda-linear maps i and pr, pr o i = id, range i = topNil (maximal ideal of Lambda) T, and the action of MvPowerSeries; the idempotent is AlgebraTools.exists_idem_topNil. The book identifies N with the range of i.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-free: Pa.Lev.freeSummand, stated for a complement C of N in M and an action of MvPowerSeries on N; Pa.Lev.OpP.freePart applies it with N the range of i and C the kernel of pr. The conclusion is an additive isomorphism with Fin rk -> MvPowerSeries / delIdeal compatible with the actions.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-quotient: Pa.Lev.OpP.quotPart, stated with MvPolynomial (sigma + sigma) R acting through act1 and an evaluation ev to the ring acting on N; the statement on the image is the equivalence of v in topNil with v in the range of j.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-splitting: Pa.Lev.OpP.spPart, with B[u] the ring Sp P ub (MvPowerSeries modulo spIdeal) and B[U] the ring MSplitAlg P n; the idempotent and the surjection are Pa.Lev.spLoc. Topological nilpotence is stated as: for every k, some power of Sp.mk (X p) carries z into m_Lambda^k times the module.
sha-hecke-ideal-tw-patching: Pa.Lev.opToTW, whose conclusion is TWRing b h ut N (R' with p, s, U, M, a, rk, e and e_smul) and TWMaps Nq ph ta with ex (theta, theta_pair, theta_coefficientMap_eq, theta_U, phi, psi, the two composites, rel1 and rel2). R' is MvPowerSeries ((Fin q x Fin n) + (Fin q x Fin n)) A.R, the module is the topologically nilpotent part from nilPart, and the variables y_{j,i} are s (X (j, i)). It assumes that O is a discrete valuation ring with IsCoef. In the proof of (7), Pa.Lev.opTransport moves the operator module from the Galois group of the augmented level to the abstract group T.GN N of the family of places, along an injective, hence bijective, map; the book identifies the two groups.
sha-hecke-ideal-jacquet: Z.Ord.OrdJac, proved by Z.Ord.ordinary_jacquet_of_literal_automorphy_n from the literature hypothesis (Bernstein-Zelevinsky finiteness and the finite length of the Jacquet module). The vector v lies in (glIwa k n).eig pi c phi; the conclusion is IsInvOn phi omega, IsSubquotient pi (PS omega) and psEig omega j = a j. The steps: the U_z-eigenvalue from uOpMul, OrdB.inv_inj for p(v) /= 0, OrdB.exists_form (through the private exists_nil of ExistsNil.lean) for the character mu and the form l, SatakeExists.isSubquotient_of_eigenform (Frobenius reciprocity), and propCp, hidx and OrdB.num for the eigenvalues. It is the part of Lemma sha-hecke-local-principal that does not use distinct characters.
sha-hecke-ideal-ordinary-point: Z.Ord.CoreOrdAlt, proved by Z.Ord.core_ordinary_of_literal_automorphy_n for an abstract Hecke set H with the universal pair of H.TK, and used for T through the private core of IsoOfDet.lean and pt_part of WJTwist.lean. The Lean's conclusion is a part Y of HSet.PartAltAlt with a property P (the cuspidal representation of autUO_of_printsH, or the PartOfAlt data of autP), D.map y = the determinant of Y.r, and for each v an omega with Y.sigma_l v a subquotient of PS omega and OrdChar for htW lam, the weight h. The local step is Z.Ord.OrdScalAlt, proved by ordinary_scalar_of_literal_automorphy_n through the private local_exp of OrdOrdScal.lean and Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-jacquet; the relation is core_eigen_of_weight_char_hecke_level (Lemma sha-hecke-local-characters). The Hida control step is Hi.spec with Z.Ord.ordinary_pt_of_literal_automorphy_n (PartPtAlt).
sha-hecke-ideal-triangular: The private flag_of_rel of OrdFlagJ.lean, through AlgebraTools.ord_ext (the relation on the group algebra), AlgebraTools.lag_triangular (Lagrange idempotents: lag_coi, and the private key with mid_zero), AlgebraTools.lag_ne_zero and AlgebraTools.coi_conj_single. The conclusion is W.HasFlag r psi.
sha-hecke-ideal-flag: Z.Ord.FlagJ, proved by Z.Ord.flagJ_alt. The Lean assumes B.RingProps Lambda J, that is all of property (1) of Proposition sha-hecke-ideal, and uses only its field O1, the characteristic polynomials at D_v; the statement assumes O1. The ordinary relations come from Ws.Eb.relKill (the universal pair's Ord with the span of an irreducible rho, AlgebraTools.Det.irrIffSpan), and the regular element from Th.Nm.regular_arithmetic_hida_of_literal_automorphy, whose private main takes s with a(s) = 1 + l and its power in the kernels of the phi_{v,j}. The private descend first factors rho through Gamma_0.
sha-hecke-ideal-conjugate: Z.Ord.ConjUnl, proved by Z.Ord.conj_unlinked_of_printed_results from the bundle Af.Hypotheses'. The Lean's hypothesis on rho is Af.AttC (weak attachment with semisimplicity) and continuity; (1) is stated with Win.Unl1 rho w' and concludes Unl psi, and (2) concludes Win.PotUnl rho w'. The polarization is UpperTheory.twistedDual_frobenius_compatibility (IsoOfFrob, Chebotarev and Brauer-Nesbitt) with satake_parameters_complex_conjugate; the conjugation of decomposition groups is CU.exists_rel (rel_one when g fixes E, rel_conj otherwise) and CU.abs_main; the comparison of two flags is CU.flag_range, by the linear independence of characters.
sha-hecke-ideal-exponents: Z.Ord.ExpTor, proved by Z.Ord.exp_torsion_of_literal_automorphy_n. The Lean states it for a cuspidal pi with ExpOf at w (every local component at w a subquotient of PS omega, with OrdChar for strictly increasing weights), and concludes Gam.TorAt pi w, Unl psi -> TU pi w, and WinAt pi t w -> the power condition; the book states the last two for one local component, and the first is the description of the supercuspidal support used in the proof. The computations are the private twist_val, link (the linked case, as in the proof of Lemma sha-hecke-ideal-above) and tors (with N = 1 + l^M from near_one).
sha-hecke-ideal-inertia: (1) is Up.diag_pt, through Up.diag_of_cong, stated in the Lean for a subgroup I of any group with a map p to Gamma_0 that sends I into the inertia group Iu u; the triviality of t_i on the kernel of chi_bar_i is shown inside the private Up.types of UpUW.lean. Teichmuller lifts are Resid.IsTeich. sha-patching-chain-cayley-closure: Killed is GDet.Kills: D.D B (1 + h * y) = 1 for every commutative algebra B and every h in B[G]. It is the kernel of [Che14, Lemma 1.19(i)] for the determinant of the group algebra (CA.d_ker relates Det.ker and Kills). The closure is closureIdeal I S for I the maximal ideal, an intersection over all natural numbers N (N = 0 gives the whole ring) and open normal subgroups; GDet.chBar D Z is closureIdeal (maximalIdeal B) (D.CH union Z), where D.CH is the set of coefficient generators of the Cayley-Hamilton ideal, and E_{D,Z} is GDet.CHQuot D Z with the quotient map GDet.toQuot. Locators in [Che14] here and in the following lemmas are those of arXiv:0809.0415v2, checked against that text.
sha-patching-chain-cayley-extension-boun: Z1 chi psi is the submodule of locally constant a : G -> k with a(gh) = chi(g) a(h) + a(g) psi(h). MultFree chi h asks for open kernels, injectivity of chi, and Module.Finite with finrank at most h for i != j. The book says extension bound where the Lean says MultFree, as multiplicity free in [Che14, Definition 2.19] is another notion. c(n,h) is finBound n h.
sha-patching-chain-cayley-bound: (1) is the content of Pa.phi_fg, which the Lean states for the open subgroup G0 of a topologically finitely generated F.Gamma: TopFG.subgroup_quot (Schreier's lemma through Group.closure_finite_fg) and the private finite_open_homs_to_finite_group. PhiCond G l, the hypothesis of (2), asks that every open subgroup have finitely many homomorphisms with open kernel to Multiplicative (ZMod l). (2) is CA.exists_multFree_of_phiCond_of_injective_chars, with h the sum of the dimensions of all the Z1(chi_i, chi_j).
sha-patching-chain-cayley-lift: CA.d_lift_idem, for a finite index type and CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents. The Lean lifts one idempotent with the Henselian property of the adically complete finite algebra A[x] (HenselianRing.is_henselian); Lemma sha-patching-chain-idempotents-lift gives the same lift. Lifting idempotents along a surjection with kernel in the radical is standard; Chenevier cites Bourbaki for it in the proof of [Che14, Theorem 2.22], and the Lean proves it.
sha-patching-chain-cayley-gma: CA.f_gma, whose conclusion IsGMA D e is: D Cayley-Hamilton, e complete orthogonal idempotents, and D.D A[X] (1 + X tensor e i) = 1 + X; with ker pi = Ring.jacobson E and pi (e i) = Pi.single i 1. The units step is CA.d_unit (IsUnit x iff IsUnit (D x), and Algebra.IsIntegral), the argument in the proof of [Che14, Lemma 2.7(i)]; the rank step uses CA.d_idem_rank, which is [Che14, Lemma 2.4(1)] over a local ring, with r the dimension r(e) of the determinant D_e there. The Lean's induction (fr_nil) starts at p = 0 and bounds dim J by the sum from p = 0; the book's sum from p = 1 drops that trivial first step.

The book's E is the quotient by the span of the Cayley-Hamilton set of GDet.ofChars chi and the h - 1, for h in an open normal subgroup inside U and the kernels; the determinant of E comes from CA.d_factor ([Che14, Lemma 1.19(ii)]), with CA.d_ch_ker ([Che14, Lemma 1.21]) and CA.d_pull for the Cayley-Hamilton property.

Their statement: F an imaginary CM field with maximal totally real subfield F+, S a finite set of primes of F+ split in F, I a set of embeddings F -> C with I and Ic together all of them, integers m_tau for tau in I, and chi an algebraic character of A_{F+}^x/(F+)^x, unramified at S, with chi_v(-1) independent of v | infinity; they give an algebraic character psi of A_F^x/F^x, unramified above S, with psi o N_{F/F+} = chi o N_{F/F+} and psi restricted to F_infinity^x equal to prod_{tau in I} tau^{m_tau} (c tau)^{w - m_tau} for some w. sha-cotangent-calculus: The rules of Alpöge's calculus in NoetherianQuotientCalc, all proved in the Lean: (1) is ruleGr and ruleFin; (2) is ruleIso; (3) is euler_additivity_of_rules (EulerAdditivityExactSequence) and ruleMono; (4) is euler_rule_two_of_graded_finite_iso (EulerIndependenceOfOrder); (5) is ruleNzd; (6) is rulePos and ruleUB, where F/(s_1,...,s_n)F is GMod.quots; (7) is Cong.chi_cong. Relation to the literature: Calc.chi is the multigraded form, taken degree by degree for large degrees, of the multiplicity symbol of Northcott and Auslander-Buchsbaum, whose inductive definition it copies [BH93, Section 4.7]. For a finitely generated module M over a noetherian local ring and elements x_1, ..., x_n with M/(x)M of finite length, the published statements are: the symbol is additive on exact sequences, independent of the order of the x_i, nonnegative, at most the length of M/(x)M, and equal to the Euler characteristic of the Koszul complex [BH93, Section 4.7], [Mat86, Section 14], [Eis95, Chapter 17]. Rules (3) to (6) are these properties with the finiteness of length replaced by admissibility and the conclusion taken for large degrees; (1) is the finiteness of graded pieces of a graded module over a standard graded algebra, and the finiteness of their length when a power of m_B R Irr kills the module; (2), (5) and (7) follow from the definition. Rule (8), additivity in a product of a degree-zero element and a homogeneous one (euler_rule_product_zero), is the additivity of the multiplicity symbol in a product, and rule (9) (ruleSmall) is the equality of the symbol with the Euler characteristic of the Koszul complex when the pieces have finite length, the Koszul complex being the alternating sum over the subsets of the list. The Lean proves the multigraded forms itself, by induction on the list, prime filtrations of graded modules (RuleDev) and the snake lemma; the text cites the published forms.
